signals.title: Polokwane International Airport: five airport police accused, arrested from 19 Oct, over 46 undocumented nationals who vanished in Apr 2025
signals.content: Police officers attached to Polokwane International Airport were arrested by the Limpopo Provincial Anti-Corruption Unit, assisted by the Polokwane Tactical Response Team, on the evening of Monday 19 October (Review Online, 19 and 20 October). Police first said five were arrested, then corrected this: three (two men and a woman aged 44 to 49) were arrested and two colleagues were still being sought (police statement via Review Online, 20 October). On Tuesday 20 October five SAPS members attached to the airport appeared in the Polokwane Magistrate's Court on charges of defeating the ends of justice and contravening section 49 of the Immigration Act, and were granted bail of R1,000 each; the case was postponed to 30 November for further investigation (Review Online, 21 October). The case is about an older incident. According to police, on 17 April 2025 a traffic officer stopped a minibus carrying 46 undocumented foreign nationals on the N1 near Polokwane; police allege that four male officers and one female officer from the airport arrived, said the station commander had arranged for the passengers to be taken to Polokwane police station, and that neither the officers nor the passengers could later be found there. These are allegations: no one has been convicted, and the accused are not named here. Case status: accused, on bail, next court date 30 November 2026. All three reports come from one outlet and rest on police statements. The pin marks the airport, where the arrests took place and where the officers work, not the April 2025 roadside stop.

signals.title: Polokwane (map point estimated): Capricorn TVET College official, 58, arrested in a police sting over an alleged R100,000 bribe, 16 Oct
signals.content: A 58-year-old official attached to Capricorn TVET College in Polokwane was arrested on Friday 16 October in a covert entrapment operation in Polokwane by the Provincial Anti-Corruption Unit, assisted by the Provincial Organised Crime Unit and the Capricorn Flying Squad (police, via Limpopo Chronicle, 16 October). Police allege he demanded a R100,000 bribe from a farmer from Senwabarwana in exchange for releasing R750,000 in project funding meant for land for the practical training of 33 students, and that he misrepresented himself as a Department of Agriculture official. During the operation the farmer handed over R40,000 in cash, which police seized. He faces charges of corruption and extortion and was expected in the Polokwane Magistrate's Court on Monday 19 October; the outcome of that appearance was not found. These are allegations: he has not been convicted and is not named here. Case status: accused, first appearance expected 19 October, outcome unknown. One public report, resting on police. The map point is estimated: the report says only 'Polokwane', so the pin is the Polokwane town point, not the place of the arrest or a college campus.

signals.title: Seshego (map point estimated): 43 learners from one school taken to hospital with stomach illness, reported 16 Oct; cause not confirmed
signals.content: The Limpopo Department of Health says 43 learners from M.E. Makgato Secondary School in Seshego were taken to hospital with stomach complaints (SABC News, 16 October). Spokesperson Neil Shikwambana said they were taken to Seshego, Helen Franz, Botlokwa and WF Knobel hospitals and that 13 were still being treated at Seshego Hospital. Briefly News, 17 October, adds that they were Grade 12 and other senior learners with acute stomach cramps and diarrhoea, that the others had been assessed and discharged, and that no deaths had been reported as of Friday 16 October. The cause is not confirmed: Briefly News reports that health authorities opened an investigation and that no definitive cause had been confirmed. When the learners fell ill is not reported. No learners are named. This is a health alert, not a crime report. Both reports rest on the health department. The map point is estimated: the school is not on the map, so the pin is the Seshego suburb point.

checked.incident: Reported by the Limpopo Department of Health on Fri 16 Oct 2026 (SABC News); when the learners fell ill is not given. The pin date is the report date.
